title: Bangladesh asks India to clarify stance on Hasina’s planned New Delhi speech
byline: Bangladesh has asked India to clarify its stance on exiled ‌former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s planned virtual address from New Delhi, warning that allowing political activities by a fugitive could hurt improving bilateral relations.

title: Motorcycle-only lanes planned on major roads
byline: The Government is set to introduce dedicated motorcycle lanes on major roads across Sri Lanka as part of a new road safety initiative aimed at reducing traffic fatalities, Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development Bimal Rathnayake said.

title: Stakeholders agree to proceed with Trincomalee oil pipeline project
byline: Key stakeholders have reached an agreement to proceed with the establishment of a new pipeline system connecting the Trincomalee oil tank farm with the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) offshore buoy, paving the way for more efficient oil transfer operations.

title: Unconvicted inmates make up over 72% of prison population
byline: Amid growing concerns over overcrowding in prisons across the country, it is identified that nearly three-fourths of inmates are remand prisoners with cases pending against them.

title: Colombo–Kandy main road at Kadugannawa reopened after rockfall
byline: The Colombo–Kandy main road, which was temporarily closed following a rockfall in the Kadugannawa area, has been reopened to traffic, police said.

title: International Association of Judges urges Sri Lanka to reconsider judges’ retirement age amendment
byline: The International Association of Judges (IAJ), the world’s oldest and largest global organisation representing judges through national judicial associations, has expressed strong concern over the Sri Lankan Government’s proposed constitutional amendment to extend the retirement age of judges by two years, warning that the manner in which the proposal has been introduced could undermine judicial independence.

title: Government mulls one-year retirement extension for Police officers
byline: The government is considering extending the retirement age of police officers with unblemished service records by one year beyond the current retirement age of 60, Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala told Parliament today.

title: Court rejects bid to obtain Chamika Karunaratne’s blood sample for DNA test
byline: The Colombo District Court today refused a request seeking an order directing Sri Lankan cricketer Chamika Karunaratne to provide a blood sample for a DNA test in connection with an ongoing paternity dispute.

title: Opposition calls for select committee to look into clearing of court cases backlog
byline: The Opposition today called for the appointment of a select committee to look into ways and means to clear the current backlog of court cases.

title: Udhayanidhi’s ’double-meaning’ remark allegedly on actor Trisha courts controversy
byline: Leader of Opposition in Tamil Nadu Assembly, Udhyanidhi Stalin courted controversy on Monday over his offensive remark, alluding to actor Trisha, Indian media reported.

title: Draft Bill to extend judges’ retirement age sent for Gazette publication: Minister
byline: The draft Bill proposing to extend the retirement age of judges by two years has been forwarded to the Department of Government Printing for publication in the Government Gazette, Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara told Parliament today.

title: Box Office history made as Spider-Man beats Endgame
byline: “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” webbed up more than $360 million during its opening weekend in the U.S. and Canada, breaking the record for the highest-grossing debut of all time. The previous record was $357 million, set by “Avengers: Endgame” in 2019, international media reported.

title: Cross talk on Auditor General’s salary increase
byline: A cross-talk arose in Parliament today between Leader of the House Bimal Ratnayake and Committee on Public Finance (COPF) Chairman Harsha de Silva over the proposal to increase the monthly salary of the Auditor General.

title: Very rough seas; fishing, naval communities told not to venture out
byline: The Department of Meteorology has warned that sea areas off the coasts from Puttalam to Pottuvil via Colombo, Galle and Hambantota will be very rough at times, with very strong gusty winds of 60 to 70 kmph.

title: Three lions die in zoo as Japan battles extreme heat
byline: Three female lions at a Tokyo zoo have died of suspected heat-related illness, as Japan battles punishing summer temperatures.

title: Dengue wards remain overcrowded despite decline in daily cases
byline: Hospitals across Sri Lanka continue to face congestion in dengue treatment wards despite a noticeable decline in the number of daily infections, hospital sources told the Daily Mirror.

title: Half-naked female image in memento stirs hornet’s nest
byline: Parents expressed concern about the memento with the image of a semi-naked female dancer awarded to the underage students who were victorious at the National Day Dhamma School competitions in the Anuradhapura District.

title: Mahanayake Theras had received wrong information: Justice Minister
byline: Claiming that the Mahanayake Theras had received wrong information regarding the extension of the retirement age of judges, Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara said yesterday that they briefed the Mahanayake Theras about the true purpose of the move.

title: Udhayanidhi Stalin released after arrest
byline: Nearly four hours after his arrest over his alleged ’’double-meaning’’ remark alluding to popular actor Trisha, Udhayanidhi Stalin was released from police custody.

title: Lanka Metro expands Colombo bus network with seven new routes
byline: Lanka Metro Transit has introduced seven new bus routes covering Colombo and its suburbs, as part of efforts to provide a more efficient, convenient and regular public transport service.

title: Man held for attempting to bribe police to free drug suspect
byline: A 29-year-old man from Thennekumbura, Kandy, has been arrested for allegedly attempting to bribe the Officer-in-Charge (OIC) of the Theldeniya Police Station with Rs. 500,000 to secure the release of a suspected drug trafficker without producing him before court.

title: Athapaththu, Harshitha lead Sri Lanka’s big ICC rankings surge
byline: Sri Lanka’s white-ball success against Pakistan has been rewarded with major gains in the latest ICC rankings, with captain Chamari Athapaththu and Harshitha Samarawickrama leading a wave of career-best rises.

title: Sri Lankans working in India can continue Sri Lanka EPF contributions
byline: Sri Lankan workers temporarily employed in India will be able to continue contributing to the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) administered by the Sri Lankan Department of Labour while being exempted from contributing to the Indian Employees’ Provident Fund under a proposed Social Security Agreement between Sri Lanka and India.

title: France wildfires reveal hundreds of WW2 shells in village
byline: Wildfires in the south of France have revealed a cache of 400 historic shells and munitions in the village of Le Porge, according to local authorities.

title: Steps initiated to develop Delft Island as sustainable tourism hub
byline: The Government has initiated steps to develop Delft Island in the Northern Province as a sustainable tourism destination, with the aim of attracting more visitors by promoting underutilised tourist locations.

title: Cabinet approves constitutional and legal amendments to strengthen judicial independence
byline: The Cabinet Ministers has approved the publication of draft amendments to the Constitution and the Judiciary Organization Act aimed at further strengthening the independence of the judiciary and expediting the disposal of pending cases.

title: New roadworthiness tests for passenger vehicles approved
byline: The Cabinet has approved the proposal to present the Motor Vehicles (Inspection) Regulations No. 03 of 2026 to Parliament for approval, introducing a formal system to test the roadworthiness of vehicles used for passenger transport and other special services.

title: India has responded to urgent request: Minister
byline: India has responded to Sri Lanka’s call for urgent assistance to control dengue and has handed over a consignment of Malathion, Minister of Health Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said.

title: More time for motorists: Expressway seatbelt grace period extended
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to extend by three months the grace period granted for the mandatory installation of seatbelts in vehicles travelling on expressways.

title: 50 low-floor buses added to Metro fleet
byline: The Cabinet has approved a proposal to procure an additional 50 comfortable low-floor buses to expand modern public transport services in urban areas, following the successful procurement of 100 such buses under the Public Transport System Modernisation Programme.

title: Cabinet nod to fast-track house arrest bill
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to expedite the drafting of legislation to introduce house arrest as a legal alternative to remand and imprisonment for eligible suspects and convicted offenders in a bid to ease overcrowding in prisons.

title: Udhayanidhi Stalin arrested over remarks on actor Trisha, DMK cries ’’vendetta’’
byline: High drama unfolded in Chennai on Tuesday morning as the Tamil Nadu Police arrested Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin from his home over remarks against actor Trisha.

title: Public urged to beware of social media extortion scams
byline: Sri Lanka Computer Emergency Readiness Team (Sri Lanka CERT) has warned the public of a fresh surge in online extortion scams carried out through Facebook Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp, with several victims already reporting incidents in recent weeks.

title: Public urged to use DMC emergency hotline 117 during heavy rains
byline: The Disaster Management Center (DMC) has urged the public to use its emergency hotline 117 to obtain information and assistance during disaster situations triggered by the prevailing heavy rains.

title: Joint Opposition urges international partners to review Anti-Corruption Bill
byline: The Joint Opposition has called on international development partners supporting Sri Lanka’s anti-corruption reforms to examine the human rights implications of the proposed Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill.

title: WhatsApp tests separate folder for business messages to reduce inbox clutter
byline: Meta-owned WhatsApp is testing a new feature designed to help users better manage business communications by automatically moving messages from large enterprises into a dedicated folder.

title: Constitution amendment to extend retirement age of judges will be implemented despite opposition protests: Minister
byline: The Constitutional amendment and the amendment to the Judicature Bill will be presented to Parliament and implemented, despite opposition protests, Minister Vijitha Herath said.

title: Two remanded over alleged multi-million rupee Customs fraud involving luxury vehicles
byline: Two suspects, including the son of the owner of a well-known gate manufacturing and motor vehicle importing company, were ordered to be remanded till August 5 by Colombo Additional Magistrate Oshadha Migara Maharachchi over allegations of evading taxes amounting to millions of rupees through the import of luxury vehicles and raw materials for the construction sector.

title: CID launches probe into SLPP General Secretary’s remarks on IGP
byline: The Acting Inspector General of Police (IGP) has instructed the Central Criminal Investigation Bureau (CCIB) to launch an investigation into a statement made by Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) General Secretary Attorney-at-Law Sagara Kariyawasam concerning the IGP.

title: Two reservoirs spill as 73 major reservoirs hold 39% capacity
byline: Only two reservoirs under the Irrigation Department were reported to be spilling as of 12.30 p.m. today, while the average storage capacity of the country’s 73 major reservoirs remained at 39.3%, the latest Water Management Division report said.

title: All schools in Hatton Education Zone closed tomorrow due to bad weather
byline: All schools under the Hatton Education Zone will remain closed tomorrow (August 5) due to prevailing adverse weather conditions.

title: Appeal Court orders resumption of Johnston Fernando corruption trial
byline: The Court of Appeal has overturned a Colombo High Court order that discharged former Minister Johnston Fernando and two former senior officials of the Cooperative Wholesale Establishment (CWE) from a corruption case, directing that the trial be resumed without further delay.

title: No opposition from Mahanayake Theras to judicial reforms: Nalinda
byline: The Mahanayake Theras did not oppose the reforms in the judicial system aiming to create efficiency and clear the backlog of cases, Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said today.

title: Daily Mirror report comes to limelight in Parliament
byline: A Daily Mirror report published on July 31 exposing the fate of the Central Expressway came to limelight in Parliament today, with Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) MP S. M. Marikkar questioning the government over losses incurred as a result of limited competition during the tender process.

title: Schools in Kandy, Nuwara Eliya to reopen tomorrow
byline: All government schools in the Kandy and Nuwara Eliya districts will reopen tomorrow (05), the Central Province Director of Education announced.

title: Metro bus service to expand to seven routes from September
byline: The Metro Bus Service will be expanded from two to seven routes from September as part of efforts to improve public passenger transport and ensure a more reliable bus service in Colombo and its suburbs, the Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development said.

title: Dehiwala shooting attempt foiled as bakery owner seizes gun
byline: A shooting attempt targeting a bakery owner near the Dahanayake Stadium on Kadawatha Road, Dehiwala, was foiled after the victim overpowered the gunman and seized his firearm, police said.

title: ’It was a rebirth for all of us’: Passengers recall chaos after Air India flight hits turbulence
byline: An Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi encountered severe turbulence on Tuesday morning, briefly losing around 300 feet in altitude and leaving at least 17 people injured, including four cabin crew members.

title: Proposed Animal Welfare Bill could destroy Sri Lankan culture
byline: The proposed Animal Welfare Bill could destroy the Buddhism based culture in Sri Lanka which has survived for more than 2500 years, UNP Chairman Wajira Abeywardena said today.

title: Eight dead, nearly 12,000 affected by adverse weather
byline: Eight people have lost their lives due to the adverse weather conditions that have affected several parts of the country over the past few days, the Disaster Management Centre (DMC) said.

title: Youth arrested for defrauding woman of Rs. 6.6M
byline: A 21-year-old suspect has been arrested by the North Western Province Unit of the Computer Crime Investigation Division for allegedly defrauding a woman of more than Rs. 6.6 million by falsely promising to secure foreign employment.

title: Rubio says US-Iran strait talks progress, deal could come ’very shortly’
byline: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday that Washington and Tehran have yet to finalize talks on passage through crucial international waterways, but he hopes an agreement will come “very shortly.”
